history.summary: Built in 1734 by Bar Raja Ambika (Queen Ambika), wife of Ahom king Swargadeo Siva Singha, on the bank of the Sivasagar (Borpukhuri) tank, which she had excavated between 1731 and 1738. It is the tallest of the trio of dols on the tank's bank (Shiva Dol, Devi Dol, Vishnu Dol) - reported as 104 ft (32 m) tall with a 195 ft base perimeter and crowned by an 8-ft golden dome (kalasha), and widely described as the tallest Shiva temple in India. Height figures conflict across sources: the Census of India Sivasagar district handbook gives both 180 ft and 104 ft in adjacent lines, and a YouTube travelogue claims 180 ft - 104 ft is the widely repeated figure. Classic Ahom (Nilachal-influenced) architecture with a four-tiered shikhara, angashikharas, and bas-relief sculptures including multi-armed Durga panels. Forms a sacred complex with Vishnu Dol and Devi Dol on the same tank bank.

name: Shiva Dol (Sivadol)
town_description: Sivasagar, about 370 km east of Guwahati, was the seat of Ahom power for nearly six centuries (capital Rangpur) and is a leading tea- and oil-producing centre. The 200-year-old Sivasagar tank (Borpukhuri) anchors the town, ringed by Ahom monuments such as Rang Ghar, Talatal Ghar and the three dols.

travel.airport: Jorhat Airport (Rowriah), about 80 km west; Dibrugarh Airport is a longer alternative
travel.road: In the heart of Sivasagar town on the bank of the Sivasagar tank; town is walkable near the tank, taxis/autos for outlying sites

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivaratri (February/March) is the biggest festival with a large mela
visitor_information.opening_hours: 7:00 AM-1:00 PM and 2:00 PM-7:30 PM (verify on visit; complex generally open 6:00 AM-6:00 PM)
